To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the evolution of the construct and definition of corporate responsibility has been a long and winding road.

(1) there has been an impressive history of evolution of definitions, (2) there has been a proliferation of definitions, (3) definitions have been expanding, (4) there has been some empirical research on definitions, (5) alternative themes have matured, (6) there has been little empirical research on definitions in recent decades, and (7) CSR continues to be a core construct but has yielded to or been transformed into alternative thematic constructs.

(1) the CSR construct has been evolving over the past five decades; (2) the evolution of the construct can be divided into four phases: the modern era (1950s), expansion (1960s), proliferation (1970s), and maturity (1980s); and (3) the evolution of CSR has been characterized by the introduction of new definitions, the development of empirical research, and the emergence of alternative thematic frameworks
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of CSR as a concept and the development of definitions.
the evolution of CSR as a construct and the evolution of alternative thematic frameworks that emerged from CSR.
the evolution of CSR and its associated themes, and the implications of this evolution for future research and practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolution of the definition of CSR is still evolving.
the CSR construct has evolved from an ambiguous and vague construct in the early 1950s to a well-defined and well-researched construct today.
the CSR construct has been and continues to evolve and change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CSR is an umbrella concept that has been transformed into a number of alternative thematic approaches, including CSP, stakeholder theory, business ethics, and sustainability.
there are many definitions for CSR, which are often used interchangeably with corporate social performance (e.g., Carroll 1999).
CSR is an evolving concept that is not static but rather dynamic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of the definition and construct has not been linear, but rather, it has been a complex and multifaceted process.
the CSR construct has evolved over the past 50 years.
the evolution of the definition of CSR has been influenced by the social and political environment.
